text:
alex (ceo): thanks for the sharp Qs in today’s all-hands. wanted to capture a slightly longer thread on our long-game positioning and immediate tradeoffs so teams have direction.

mira (vp-product): huge thanks. PMs asked for a "north star" paragraph we can put at the top of PRDs that clarifies where Redwood must stay distinct in 18 months. any leaders want to draft a sentence?

alex (ceo): draft north star: "Redwood enables teams to ship LLM-driven features with predictable latency, transparent unit economics, and consistent operational controls across cloud-hosted, reserved, and private deployments." that should anchor PRDs and external messaging.

lee (cto): engineering addendum for PRDs: emphasize "single runtime contract" (same API & behavior across modes) and "ops-grade fallbacks" (automated routing to compatible model variants when capacity is tight). keeps expectations aligned.

jamal (head-sales): useful. sales follow-up: when customers ask "why not just run models ourselves?" what's the crisp economic answer? we need a sentence for decks.

alex (ceo): reply for decks: "We remove the operational heavy lifting — optimized runtime, batching/caching, and reliable routing — so teams avoid hidden costs of building and running inference at scale." add a short ROI bullet with 3-5% example savings if possible.

anya (research): curious about competitor framing. should SEs call out competitors by name in initial outreach, or use contrast statements? some reps want a direct comparison doc.

mira (vp-product): prefer contrast language publicly. SEs can use a private competitor matrix for technical objections. marketing to make both: public contrast lines + private matrix.

kai (senior-eng): roadmap clarity Q: kernel/runtime perf vs product ergonomics. engineering needs a deterministic rule for sprint swaps when a deal surfaces. can leadership specify a threshold?

alex (ceo): yes. rule: any anonymized deal > $X ARR that requires a measurable perf target (e.g., p50 < 60ms at defined QPS) triggers expedited runtime work. smaller deals: prefer product/ops changes that reduce friction. product to publish the anonymized deal list weekly.

jamal (head-sales): please ensure that list includes an estimated close date and why perf matters (latency, isolation, legal). helps prioritization.

mira (vp-product): will do. ops-bot: can you create the task for product-ops to publish the one-pager, the SE appendix, and the anonymized deals list?

ops-bot: created task T-7773 in #product-ops: "Publish north-star PRD paragraph, exec deck line, SE appendix, and anonymized prioritized deals list" assigned to @mira, due in 4 business days.

alex (ceo): last bit on messaging: when contrasting other vendors, lead with outcome (what customer gets) rather than tech jargon. e.g., "We give you a single API and production economics so your app runs predictably at scale" beats a long list of features.

mira (vp-product): agreed. marketing, can you produce two headline packs: "outcome-first" and "engineer-first" variants? post in #marketing and tag product for review.

jamal (head-sales): and pls include a short rebuttal for the "cheaper to self-host" objection with a 2-line cost-risk example.

anya (research): i'll add a tiny bench test doc that SEs can use privately (latency CDFs, cost model sketch).

kai (senior-eng): thx. last engineering ask: if we re-prioritize runtime perf, will we get comms so we can replan sprints?

alex (ceo): yes  product flags a perf-driven deal, leadership will confirm within 48 hours and product will publish the sprint swap. if anyone has urgent blockers, DM me.

mira (vp-product): will follow up with drafts and link them here. thanks all  let's keep this focused and iterate quickly. :thumbsup:
